Wadowice Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Wadowice, Poland

Not demolished. Wadowice's Jewish community, settled from the second half of the 19th century, numbered 1,437 people (20.9 percent of the town) by 1921, most killed by the Germans at Bełżec and Auschwitz-Birkenau between 1942 and 1943. This cemetery, established in 1882, was purchased by a German entrepreneur during WWII, with its funeral house partially damaged; burials continued after 1945. A monument marks the mass grave of 92 people murdered in 1943 in Maków Podhalański, exhumed and reburied here in 1964; the last funeral took place in 1990.
